title: Memory-bounded IQP amplitude contraction
difficulty_explanation: The solver must recognize a shuffled low-treewidth IQP factor graph, produce a checkable bounded-width elimination certificate, and execute selected 72-qubit amplitudes with a custom TensorCircuit contraction instead of a dense statevector.

seed_protocol.base_seed_mapping: The single base seed initializes one NumPy Generator stream that emits the two ordered IQP cases and private oracle orders.
seed_protocol.determinism_scope: Exact public case bytes are deterministic only under the pinned image/runtime and are identified by the evaluator-emitted case_digest; private oracle orders are excluded.
seed_protocol.case_identity: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted keys and compact separators over the ordered exact public IQP cases; functional stdout emits the full case_digest and protocol_seed in one structured orbit_q_case_identity JSON line.
seed_protocol.pinned_numpy_note: The target image pins NumPy 2.2.6; a seed alone is not a cross-runtime case identity, so trial manifests must bind the image/runtime and case_digest.

contract.hidden_case_source: explicit evaluator --seed, otherwise verifier-only ORBIT_Q_CANDIDATE_SEED, legacy ORBIT_CONTRACTION_SEED, or local default 1072026
contract.determinism_scope: trial manifests bind the pinned image and evaluator-emitted case_digest; a seed alone is not a cross-runtime case identity
contract.anti_hardcoding: The seed changes graph relabelings, all circuit angles, and selected output strings; oracle amplitudes and planted elimination orders are not passed to the solution.
contract.oracle: Independent complex128 NumPy variable elimination on the IQP Ising factor graph, with a separate tiny dense-sum identity canary

difficulty_levers: 72 qubits, ruling out dense statevector materialization
shuffled cylindrical-grid labels that conceal the planted sweep order
twelve selected complex amplitudes per hidden case, making contraction-path reuse operationally necessary
TensorCircuit custom-contractor execution with reusable paths
claim_boundary: The expert and evaluator are validated prototypes. No solver-model trial has been run and no model-hardness claim is made.
api_risks: Circuit.rzz follows exp(-i theta Z tensor Z / 2); a convention drift changes every factor phase.
Circuit.amplitude_before returns copied TensorNetwork nodes whose ordering is reused by an explicit path only for identical circuit topology.
TensorCircuit's OMECo adapter is an installed API but remains an optional dependency; the pinned image currently supplies omeco==0.2.0.
OMECo TreeSA path search is stochastic; only independently checked amplitudes and logical-width certificates are scored, with complex tolerances validated across hidden seeds.
TensorCircuit backend, dtype, and global contractor state are process-global; the expert uses a local contractor and complex128.
